summary: This program stores three numbers in variables, adds them together into a fourth variable, and prints the total. It is a first look at how a program holds values and combines them.

lines.code: # Add three numbers and print the result
lines.text: A comment is a note for people reading the code; Python ignores every line that starts with #, so it costs nothing to say what the program is for.
The = sign is an assignment, not a claim of equality: it puts the value 5 into a variable named num1 so the rest of the program can refer to it by name.

Python works out the right-hand side first, adding the three stored values, and only then stores the answer in result. Naming the total instead of adding inside the print keeps the calculation and the display separate.
Passing two things to print, separated by a comma, makes Python print them side by side with a space between, so you get a label and the number without any string juggling.
